key_insight: ChronoSyn uses the historical order of materials discovery as additional supervision to improve predictions of which hypothetical compositions can be synthesized.
engineering_relevance: More effective synthesizability screening could help prioritize experimental targets from large computational and generative materials searches.
method: Learn a shared representation of material composition.
Jointly predict synthesizability and the relative reporting order of known materials.
Score hypothetical compositions to identify promising chemical families.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved prediction over baseline models and screening of approximately 50 million hypothetical compositions, with high-scoring families including experimentally reported compositions unseen during training.
watch_item: Reporting chronology may reflect research priorities and experimental access as well as synthesizability, so prospective experimental validation remains important.
paper_title: Learning the Chronology of Materials Discovery for Synthesizability Prediction
